newsitem.title: USA: Arco increases estimates on N.Slope field.
newsitem.headline: Arco increases estimates on N.Slope field.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co's ARCO Alaska Inc Wednesday said it increased its estimates of proven and potential reserves at the new Alpine oil field on Alaska's North Slope.

As a result of extensive reservoir studies and preparation of a reservoir depletion plan, ARCO said it now estimates reserves of 365 million barrels upon full development of the field, including its peripheral areas. Earlier estimates, made last year when the field was declared commercial, were 250 to 300 million barrels.
Estimates of peak production have also been increased to 70,000 barrels per day (bpd) in the year 2001, up 10,000 bpd from the previous estimate. Initial production of 40,000 bpd is expected in 2000.

Alpine, located 34 miles west of the Kuparuk River oil field, is 56 percent-owned by ARCO Alaska Inc, 22 percent owned by Anadarko Petroleum Corp and 22 percent owned by Union Texas Petroleum Holdings Inc.

Arco said development of the project is expected to cost $650 million. Earlier this week ARCO's board of directors approved ARCO's $364 million portion of the project and work is expected to begin in December, pending co-owner approval and receipt of necessary permits.

Initial development plans call for the drilling of 50 wells and the installation of associated facilities. After the field is put on production, additional wells targeting the periphery of the field may be drilled. Arco said this could require an additional investment of $100 million.
